title: Barney Josephson and Cafe Society
summary: Hall says John Hammond really made Cafe Society and tells of Josephson snubbing Albert Ammons.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And so after many, many years you found yourself working again for Barney Josephson, who went back to the Cafe Society in Teddy Wilson's sextet.

Right. Right. Barney Joseph con thinks he's an impresario, but he didn't do it himself. John Hammond did it for him. He would take the credit now, but when I was hired that isn't the way I saw it in 1940.

I can remember one night Albert Ammons, the (inaudible) Boogie-woogie pianist (inaudible) came in. Barney was standing at the door, and Albert spoke to him. Barney didn't answer him, and he came back to the dressing room crying (inaudible). And we gave him hell. Don't speak to him anymore.
